title: 4-Digit by 2-Digit Division Word Problems
intro: Teach division with two-digit divisors using estimates and labeled groups.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Begin with a convenient multiple of the divisor and adjust it. Choose an activity that matches whether you want students to find group size, group count, or a remainder.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

1,237 ÷ 24 = 51 R 13

Account for every counter using partial quotients
StepFull groupsCounters usedCounters left
First chunk5024 × 50 = 1,20037
Next chunk124 × 1 = 2413

Add the partial quotients: 50 + 1 = 51 groups.
Check the total: 24 × 51 + 13 = 1,237 counters.

Ask your student

What does the quotient count in this activity?

If your student needs help

If the estimate is too large, compare its product with the dividend and revise it together.
